transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, yeah, so I'm here because... well, honestly, everything is just a complete disaster right now. I feel like I absolutely cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. It's like, I try, I really do, but it's just impossible to keep it all straight. 

I started this little shop making these cute little hair clips and charms and things, which I really love doing, but the supplies are just everywhere. Like, my entire desk and half my floor are just covered in beads and wire and packaging materials, and then right in the middle of all that mess are my assignment notes for my classes. And I try to keep track of it all, I really do, but all my due dates for school and all my shipping receipts for the shop just end up in these massive, overwhelming piles. 

I'll sit down and try to figure out what I'm supposed to be doing, and I just stare at these mountains of paper and supplies, and I honestly don't know what to do first. It's just so frustrating because I have all these great ideas for the shop, and obviously I need to get my schoolwork done so I don't fail, but the physical stuff is just taking over my room. I just sit there completely paralyzed by the piles. Like, I'll buy a planner to get it together, but then the planner gets lost under a pile of assignment notes and bubble mailers, and then I'm right back to where I started, just totally overwhelmed by the mess and not knowing where to even begin with any of it.
Has this struggle with organization and focus been something you've dealt with since you were a child, or is this a more recent problem for you?

Oh, um, wow, since I was a child? Yeah, it’s definitely not a new thing, not at all. I mean, my mom actually—she has this huge plastic storage bin of all my old school stuff, you know, like macaroni artwork and report cards and just random papers from when I was really little. And she literally still has these specific notes from my elementary school teachers saved in there. It’s actually kind of embarrassing now when we look back at it, because the notes were always, always saying the exact same things, year after year. 

Like, my teachers would write to her saying I was constantly out of my seat. Just wandering around the classroom, going over to the pencil sharpener or looking out the window when we were supposed to be doing silent reading or sitting cross-legged on the rug. And I would always, always be talking before the teacher even called on me. Like, they'd ask a question and I’d just blurt out the answer because I just couldn't hold it in and wait for them to pick someone, or I'd just start talking about something completely unrelated to the lesson. 

And the group activities! Oh my gosh, I remember I would just rush through them so fast. The teachers would write in those notes that I was just speeding through the group work, leaving the other kids behind. And the thing is, it wasn't that I didn't get it—the teachers even said I completely understood the work we were supposed to be doing! I just couldn't bring myself to slow down and do it at the same pace as everyone else. I just had to get it done right that exact second, or I'd get so incredibly impatient. So, yeah, it’s definitely been a thing forever. My mom still brings up those notes sometimes, but honestly, it was just how I always was, constantly moving and talking and just rushing through every single thing they gave me...
